correctness.rationale: All essential inferences and computations in DRAFT.md §2 were independently recomputed and hold. Witness bitstring '+---++++---+---+---+--+-++-++' has length 29, a0=+1, is reciprocal-canonical under stated numeric lex-min rule (a1 -1 vs +1 for reverse '++-++-+--+---+---+---++++---+'), and satisfies skew-symmetry a_{14+k}=(-1)^k a_{14-k}. Exact integer autocorrelations recomputed as [0,-3,0,1,0,1,0,1,0,-3,0,-3,0,-3,0,-3,0,1,0,1,0,1,0,1,0,-3,0,1], sumsq 62, merit Fraction 841/124 ≈6.7822580645 — matches. P(i)=3-6i via even/odd sums gives |P(i)|^2=45 exactly, so M>=sqrt(45)=6.7082039325. Lipschitz lemma |P(e^{it})-P(e^{is})|<=406|t-s| (L=sum_{k=0}^{28}k=406) and modulus corollary plus spacing pi/N are correct; grid maxima recomputed via numpy FFT and independent direct summation agree to ~7e-15: 6.708203932499369 stable at N=16384,65536,262144,1048576 (attained at z=±i, which are grid nodes when 4|N, true for all N used), giving upper 6.713070528 at N=262144 and 6.709421331 at N=2^20 (+1e-6 margin), so interval width <0.005/<0.0013 and corollary min M<=6.7095 holds at N=2^20. Exhaustive 16384 skew scan recomputed independently in exact integers: min sumsq 62, max merit 841/124, exactly 4 attainers {115,1144,4397,5414} as two reciprocal pairs, with witness mask 1144; census CSV has 16384 rows, min sumsq 62, same attainers, sampled grid/sumsq spot-checks match. 1-flip local optimality at N=8192 re-verified (no improvement) and 2-flip exhaustive (378 pairs) also shows no grid improvement, consistent with DRAFT §3 context. Draft correctly distinguishes proof from experimental evidence (§3 basin-hopping/hill-climbs reported as context only, §5 limitations disclaim record comparison, full sweep, interval arithmetic, and M=sqrt(45) equality). Residual float-margin gap (FFT doubles +1e-6 vs interval arithmetic) is explicitly disclosed and factually safe (observed error ~1e-14, margin 1e-6 is 5 orders larger; worst-case N log N eps bound ~1e-11), so not a hidden error. Minor topic-level count 2^28/2=134217728 ignores 16384 palindromic fixed points (true reciprocal orbits (2^28+2^14)/2=134225920) but DRAFT does not rely on exact count for any proof.

originality.rationale: Substantive comparison to cutoff-known nearest priors shows no prior that implies the packaged joint certificate. (1) Balister et al. 2020 (arXiv:1907.09488) proves asymptotic existence of ultraflat families with sup<=(1+o1)sqrt(n) but gives no explicit degree-28 witness, no merit value, no certificate — opposite end (existential vs explicit). (2) Borwein-Choi (arXiv:math/0005094) + Mossinghoff database are the heuristic/stochastic tables that would contain R28_sup/R28_F; they lack FFT-prefiltered exhaustive quotient, Lipschitz-rigorous sup upper bounds, exact Fraction merit, and joint sup+merit reporting with replayable verifier — delta is evidence strength (heuristic value vs proved interval+exhaustive subspace proof), even if numeric bitstring coincidentally appeared before. (3) Borwein-Choi-Jedwab 2004 merit>6.34 infinite families are asymptotic constructions, not finite-N=29 joint sup+merit optima with sup certificate — complementary. Internal SCOPE scan (3 success hits on 4-uniform families, J2-free ranks, spider walks; 4 failure hits on Szemeredi-Trotter, Polya-Vinogradov, Z_197 bases, dicyclic gaps) is disjoint in objects/methods. Live web re-verification was attempted via webfetch for arXiv 1907.09488 and Wikipedia Littlewood polynomial but both returned transport errors in this offline workspace, so priority cannot be live-confirmed; however no substantive duplication was found in available sources. Residual risk remains that the 29-bit string or sumsq-62 optimum already appears in stale heuristic rows (16k skew space is trivially enumerable and prior authors likely visited it), but the two-sided interval sqrt(45)<=M<=sqrt(45)+0.00122 plus exact subspace-maximum proof with verifier has not been shown to be previously published in that certified form, so novelty as a certificate passes the low bar for originality even though value fails.

value.rationale: Even taking correctness and certificate-novelty as given, the result is not independently worth finding later under SCOPE value filters. Target claim (topic.json) required a joint record-beater: certified M<=R28_sup-0.03 or F>=R28_F+0.20 with 3% non-regression vs pinned Borwein-Choi/Mossinghoff records. DRAFT §5(i) explicitly states this is 'unassessed, not achieved' (offline, records unpinned). Fallback required (a) certified complete census over canonical representatives (134M orbits) plus extension to degrees 24-27 and (b) certified non-existence gap B28>=min(R28_sup,5.95). Delivered is only a 16384-row skew census (0.012% of canonical space, 2^14 vs 2^28/2), no full sweep, no gap, no 24-27 extension. What IS delivered — single-witness one-sided bounds min_{L28}M<=6.7095 and max_{L28}F>=841/124 plus exact optimum over the tiny skew subspace — leaves global interval [5.385,6.7095] for min M wide (L2 lower bound sqrt(29)=5.385) with unknown distance to true optimum, and no record context to show 6.708/6.782 is globally good (random-polynomial sup ~9-10, random merit ~1, so better than random but unquantified vs optimum; heuristic non-beating searches are explicitly non-proofs). This collapses to a degree-28-specific single example (mere parameter instantiation) plus a <1s trivial enumeration (16384 integer sums) without theoretical insight, i.e. tiny unmotivated enumeration and textbook Lipschitz+autocorrelation exercise applied to one bitstring. A later researcher seeking flat polynomials would not cite this as a record, gap, or method; at most as one heuristic example among many. Hence correct and arguably new, but must be rejected per 'reject textbook restatements, mere parameter substitutions, tiny unmotivated gains, and unexplained enumerations even if correct and new.'
